title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is describing the closure of a boundary stratum M_[G] of the Deligne–Mumford compactification \hat M_{g,ν}. Here G is a stable graph of numerical type (g,ν). S is its vertex set; note that the same letter S is also used for the base scheme. Each vertex α carries a genus g_α and a set \hat I_α of 'points'. These points are the legs from I together with the half-edges at α. The previous page defines \hat M_G := ∏_α \hat M_{g_α,\hat I_α}.

Formula (31) on this page says that \hat M_G represents the fibred groupoid S ↦ {families (Y_α)_{α} of stable (DM) curves over S, Y_α of genus g_α, with a monomorphism (\hat I_α)_S ↪ Y_α^{smooth}}.

Formulas (32)–(33): put \hat I = ⊔ \hat I_α = I ⊔ Ã, where Ã is the set of half-edges (oriented edges), with involution σ_Ã, and Y = ⊔ Y_α. This gives a monomorphism \hat I_S ↪ Y^{smooth}.

Formula (34): glue each pair of sections exchanged by σ_Ã, X̂ = Y/(σ_Ã)_S. The result is again a stable curve over S. Its genus is Σ g_α + b_1(G).

Formula (35): the sections indexed by I survive in the smooth locus, so (X̂, I_S) is a stable I-pointed curve.

Formula (36): hence a canonical morphism of 'multiplicités' (stacks) \hat M_G → \hat M_{g,I}. In modern terms this is Knudsen's clutching/gluing morphism ξ_G. A marginal NB says it is a local immersion (unramified) but not an immersion: it factors through \hat M_G/Γ, Γ = Aut G. It is equivariant for the action of Γ on \hat M_G and on \hat M_{g,I} via Γ → 𝔖_I.

The next page passes to the stack quotients: [\hat M_G/Γ] → [\hat M_{g,I}/𝔖_I] = \hat M_{g,ν}. This is meant to describe the closure of the stratum M_[G] and its specializations [G'], which are the strata coming from the boundary of \hat M_G.
errors: Notational clash: S denotes both the vertex set of G (α∈S) and the base scheme S in the functor of points. This is harmless but confusing.

Not on this page but directly dependent on it: the next page asserts that the induced map [\hat M_G/Γ] → \hat M_{g,ν} is a closed immersion. In general this is false. The clutching map is finite and unramified, and onto the closure of the stratum, but generally not injective. It is the normalization of the stratum closure, and boundary strata closures self-intersect. Example: over a curve with two non-separating nodes, the map [\hat M_{g-1,ν+2}/𝔖_2] → Δ_irr has two preimages. The NB on this page ('imm. locale, mais pas une immersion') is correct; the 'encore une immersion, fermée cette fois-ci' on the next page overstates it, unless one restricts to graphs where the issue does not arise.

ideas.what: Product of compactified moduli spaces over vertices of a stable graph, representing systems of pointed stable curves
ideas.modern_name: \bar M_G = ∏_v \bar M_{g(v),n(v)}, the 'vertex moduli' of a stable graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knudsen (1983); systematized by Kontsevich–Manin and Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the stratification of \hat M_{g,ν} and the Teichmüller tower qualitatively, without this explicit construction

ideas.what: Gluing pairs of sections via the edge involution to get the stable curve X̂ and the clutching morphism \hat M_G → \hat M_{g,I}, equivariant for Aut G → 𝔖_I
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knudsen (Projectivity of the moduli space of stable curves II, 1983); Deligne–Mumford 1969 for the boundary

ideas.what: Observation that the clutching map is unramified (local immersion) but not an immersion, factoring through the quotient by Γ = Aut G
ideas.modern_name: ξ_G is finite unramified; [\bar M_G/Aut G] → \bar M_{g,n} is the normalization of the stratum closure

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean but standard construction of Knudsen's clutching morphisms indexed by stable graphs, written in Grothendieck's 'multiplicités' language. It is historically nice as an independent treatment, but contains nothing absent from the literature. Its main idiosyncrasy is the closed-immersion claim on the next page, which is actually incorrect in general.
transcription_corrections: The first equation label is (31), not (32): it continues '\hat M_G représente le groupoïde fibré' from the previous page. The \hat I = ... / Y = ... system is (32), not (33). Only the mono \hat I_S ↪ Y^lisse is (33).
In (35) and the following line the curve is \hat X (with hat): '(\hat X, \hat I_S) devient une courbe MD sur S'.
In (34) the subscript is (σ_Ã)_S, i.e. the involution on Ã taken over S.
The NB reads approximately: 'NB Ce morphisme est une imm. locale, mais pas une immersion [il se factorise par un morphisme ... \hat M_G/Γ ... provenant de l'action de Γ = Aut G]'.
